intro: Many families in Chicago have a special book at home. For Muslim families, that book is the Qur'an. It is kept with care. It is read out loud. Its letters are Arabic. In this unit you will learn what the Qur'an is.
You will meet Amira and Yusuf. You will see how their families hold the book. You will learn what a surah is. You will learn what an ayah is. You will find surahs named for a bee and an elephant.
We will use fair words. We will say "Muslims believe." We will say "the Qur'an says." That way we learn about the book. And we are kind to every friend.
bigQuestion: What is the Qur'an, and how do Muslim families read and care for it?

timeline.t: Wash your hands and dry them well
Take the Qur'an down from the high shelf
Unwrap the cloth or open the case with care
Open the book from the right side
Find the surah by its name
Read the ayahs out loud, one by one
Wrap it up and put it back on the high shelf

words.d: the holy book of Muslims; the name means the reading
a person who follows the religion called Islam
the man Muslims believe God gave the Qur'an to
the language the Qur'an is written in, read right to left
a chapter of the Qur'an; there are 114 of them
one line, or verse, of the Qur'an; the word also means sign
The Opening, the first surah; it has seven ayahs
to say words out loud, often from memory

test.why: The Qur'an is the holy book of Muslims, who follow Islam.

test.q: Who do Muslims believe received the words of the Qur'an?
test.why: Muslims believe God gave the Qur'an to Muhammad, a prophet.

test.q: What language is the Qur'an written in?
test.why: The Qur'an is written in Arabic and read from right to left.
Arabic goes right to left, so a Qur'an opens from the right.
Wudu is the washing many Muslims do before they pray or read the Qur'an.

test.q: How is the Qur'an usually read?
test.why: Muslims recite the Qur'an out loud, and the voice goes up and down.
A surah is a chapter of the Qur'an. An ayah is a line.

Which surah is named for an animal?
test.why: The Elephant is surah 105. The Cow, The Bee and The Ant are animal names too.

write.prompt: Draw or tell: How does a Muslim family care for the Qur'an? Use two things from the unit. You could use Al-Fatiha (1:1-7) or The Ant (27:18). Say what the book says, and say what Muslims believe about it.
tips: Start your sentence with "Muslims believe" or "the Qur'an says."
Name the surah you talk about.
Use a unit word, like surah or ayah.
Tell one way a family shows care for the book.

title: A Book Called the Qur'an

chapters.title: What the Qur'an Is
chapters.bigQuestion: What is the Qur'an, and how do Muslim families treat it?

story.title: The Green Book on the Top Shelf
story.kicker: Amira's grandfather reaches for a book that is kept higher than all the other books.
paragraphs: Amira is six. She lives in Chicago with her family. Today her grandfather is visiting. He walks to the tall bookshelf in the living room. He reaches up to the very top shelf. There is a green book there, wrapped in soft cloth.

"Wait," Grandfather says with a smile. "First we wash our hands." They go to the sink together. They wash their hands and dry them well. Then Grandfather takes the book down. He unwraps the cloth with care.
The book has gold letters on the cover. "This is the Qur'an," Grandfather says. "It is our holy book." He opens it from the right side. The letters inside curl and loop. They are Arabic letters.

Grandfather does not read quietly. He reads out loud. His voice goes up and down, almost like a song. Amira sits close and listens. When he is done, he wraps the book again. He puts it back on the top shelf.
story.think: Why do you think Amira's family keeps the green book on the highest shelf?

lessons.title: The Holy Book of Muslims
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an is the holy book of people called Muslims.
reading: A *holy book* is a book a religion loves. Many religions have one. Muslims are people who follow the religion of Islam. Their holy book is the Qur'an.
Muslims read the Qur'an at home. They read it at the mosque. A mosque is a place where Muslims pray. Many Muslims know parts of it by heart.
You can say the name like this: kur-AHN. The word is Arabic. It means "the reading" or "the reciting." Reciting is saying words out loud.

words.d: a book that a religion treats as very special
a person who follows the religion called Islam

look.title: Three Holy Books
look.text: Picture three books on a table. One is the Torah. Jewish families read it. One is the Bible. Christian families read it. One is the Qur'an. Muslim families read it. Each book is special to the people who read it.
look.prompt: Which book on the table do Muslim families read? How do you know?

check.q: What is the Qur'an?
choices: A book of songs for school
check.why: The Qur'an is the holy book of Muslims, the people who follow Islam.

check.q: Who reads the Qur'an as their holy book?
check.why: Muslims read the Qur'an. Jewish families read the Torah and Christians read the Bible.

check.q: What does the word Qur'an mean?
check.why: Qur'an is an Arabic word. It means the reading or the reciting.

lessons.title: Words from God, Muslims Believe
lessons.mainIdea: Muslims believe the words of the Qur'an came from God to a man named Muhammad.
reading: Muslims believe the Qur'an came from God. They believe God sent the words to a man. His name was Muhammad. He lived a long time ago in a desert land.
Muslims say Muhammad was a *prophet*. A prophet is a person who brings a message. Muslims believe his message was the Qur'an. Many Muslims say a blessing after his name.
In this class we say "Muslims believe." People believe different things. We learn what Muslims believe. We are kind about what everyone believes.

words.d: a person who brings a message; Muslims say Muhammad was a prophet
the man Muslims believe God gave the Qur'an to

look.title: How the Qur'an Begins
look.text: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds,
look.cite: Qur'an 1:2, Surah Al-Fatiha (The Opening), Marmaduke Pickthall translation, 1930
look.prompt: Allah is the Arabic word for God. Who is this line talking about?

check.q: Who do Muslims believe the Qur'an came from?
check.why: Muslims believe God sent the words of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

check.q: Who do Muslims say received the words?
check.why: Muslims believe the words of the Qur'an were given to Muhammad.

check.q: What is a prophet?
choices: A person who brings a message
check.why: A prophet is a person who brings a message. Muslims say Muhammad was a prophet.

lessons.title: Written in Arabic
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an is written in a language called Arabic.
reading: Open a Qur'an. The letters curl and loop. They are not English letters. They are *Arabic* letters. Arabic is a language spoken in many countries.
Muslims believe the Qur'an came in Arabic. So they read it in Arabic. Many Muslims do not speak Arabic at home. They learn the Arabic words anyway.
The Qur'an has been put into English too. That is called a translation. But Muslims say the Arabic is the real Qur'an.

words.d: the language the Qur'an is written in
the same words put into a different language

look.title: Two Kinds of Letters
look.text: Look at the word GOD in English. It has three straight, plain letters. Now picture the Arabic word Allah. It looks like a line with a loop, a tall stroke and a little curve. It means God. Both words point to the same idea, but they look very different on the page.
look.prompt: How are Arabic letters different from the letters you write at school?

check.q: What language is the Qur'an written in?
check.why: The Qur'an is written in Arabic. Muslims believe it came in Arabic.

check.q: What is a translation?
choices: The same words in a new language
check.why: A translation puts words into a different language, like Arabic into English.

check.q: Which do Muslims say is the real Qur'an?
check.why: Muslims say the Arabic Qur'an is the real Qur'an. Translations help people understand it.

lessons.title: Reading from Right to Left
lessons.mainIdea: Arabic is read from right to left, so a Qur'an opens from the other side.
reading: English goes from left to right. Arabic goes the other way. You read from *right to left*. Your eyes start on the right side of the page.
So a Qur'an opens from the right. The front cover is where you expect the back. Page one is on the right side. You turn pages toward the left.
This can feel strange at first. Try it with any book. Open it from the back. Now you know how a Qur'an opens.

words.d: the way Arabic is read, starting on the right side of the page

look.title: Which Way Do They Go?
look.unit: 1 = left to right, 2 = right to left
look.cite: Writing directions of these four languages, as taught in any beginning language book
look.prompt: Which two languages go the same way as Arabic and English? Find each pair.

check.q: Which way is Arabic read?
check.why: Arabic is read from right to left. English is read from left to right.

check.q: Where is page one in a Qur'an?
check.why: Because Arabic goes right to left, a Qur'an opens from the right.

check.q: Which language goes the same way as English?
check.why: Spanish goes left to right, like English. Arabic and Hebrew go right to left.

lessons.title: A High Shelf and Clean Hands
lessons.mainIdea: Many Muslim families keep the Qur'an high up, wrapped or in a case, and wash before reading.
reading: Many Muslim families keep the Qur'an on a high shelf. Nothing is put on top of it. It is often wrapped in cloth. Some keep it in a *case* or on a stand.
Before reading, many Muslims wash. They wash hands, face, arms and feet. This washing is called *wudu*. It is a way of getting ready.
These are ways of showing respect. Respect means treating something as important. Not every family does it the same way. But the care is the same.

words.d: the washing many Muslims do before prayer or reading the Qur'an
a box or cover that keeps a book safe
treating a person or thing as important

look.title: Getting Ready to Read
look.text: Picture a small wooden stand shaped like an X. A Qur'an rests open on it. Next to it is a folded cloth. A boy comes in with wet, clean hands. He dries them on a towel before he touches the page.
look.prompt: What did the boy do before touching the book? Why do you think he did that?

check.q: Where do many Muslim families keep the Qur'an?
check.why: Many families keep it on a high shelf with nothing on top of it, to show respect.

check.q: What is wudu?
check.why: Wudu is the washing many Muslims do before they pray or read the Qur'an.

check.q: Why do families wrap the Qur'an in cloth?
choices: To show respect and keep it safe
check.why: Wrapping the book, like the high shelf, is a way of showing respect.

lessons.title: A Book That Is Sung
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an is read out loud, and the reading often sounds like singing.
reading: Most books are read quietly. The Qur'an is different. Muslims read it out loud. This is called *reciting*. The voice goes up and down.
Some people recite very well. Their voices are slow and clear. It can sound like a song. People sit still and listen.
Children learn to recite too. They start with short parts. They say them again and again. Soon they know them by heart.

words.d: to say words out loud, often from memory
knowing words so well you can say them without looking

look.title: One Short Line
look.text: Say: He is Allah, the One!
look.cite: Qur'an 112:1, Surah Al-Ikhlas (Sincerity), Marmaduke Pickthall translation, 1930
look.prompt: This line is very short. Why might a short line be easy to learn by heart?

check.q: How do Muslims usually read the Qur'an?
check.why: The Qur'an is recited out loud. The reading often sounds like a song.

check.q: What does recite mean?
check.why: To recite is to say words out loud, often from memory.

check.q: Which parts do children learn first?
check.why: Children start with short parts and repeat them until they know them by heart.

lessons.title: Muslim Families in Chicago
lessons.mainIdea: Many Muslim families live in Chicago, and the Qur'an is read in homes all over the city.
reading: Chicago is a big city in Illinois. Many kinds of families live here. Many of them are Muslim. Some came from far away. Some were born here.
There are many *mosques* in Chicago. A mosque is where Muslims pray together. The Qur'an is read there every day. Children go to learn it too.
You might have a Muslim friend. Maybe there is a Qur'an in their home. Now you know what it is.

words.d: a building where Muslims pray together
a big city in Illinois where many Muslim families live

look.title: A Street in the City
look.text: Picture one city block. There is a church with a steeple. There is a temple with a star on the door. There is a mosque with a round roof called a dome. Families walk into each one. Inside each one, people read a holy book.
look.prompt: Which building do Muslim families walk into? What book is read inside?

check.q: What is a mosque?
check.why: A mosque is the building where Muslims pray together and read the Qur'an.

check.q: Which is true about Chicago?
check.why: Chicago has many kinds of families, and many of them are Muslim.

check.q: What state is Chicago in?
check.why: Chicago is a big city in the state of Illinois.

lessons.title: Saying It the Fair Way
lessons.mainIdea: We say "Muslims believe" and "the Qur'an says" so everyone is treated fairly.
reading: People believe many different things. In school we learn about all of them. We do not say who is right. We say what each group believes.
So we say "Muslims believe." We say "the Qur'an says." These words are *fair*. They tell what the book says. They let each person decide.
Try it now. Say, "Muslims believe the Qur'an came from God." That is a fair sentence. It is true about what Muslims believe.

words.d: treating every person and every belief with the same respect

look.title: Two Ways to Say It
look.text: Sentence A: "The Qur'an came from God." Sentence B: "Muslims believe the Qur'an came from God." Sentence B tells us who believes it. It works for every student in the room, no matter what their family believes.
look.prompt: Which sentence would you use in class? Why is it the fair one?

check.q: Which sentence is the fair way to say it in class?
choices: Everyone knows the Qur'an is true
Muslims believe the Qur'an came from God
check.why: Saying "Muslims believe" tells who believes it and treats everyone fairly.

check.q: What do the words "the Qur'an says" do?
choices: Tell where the book is kept
check.why: "The Qur'an says" reports what is in the book without telling anyone what to believe.

check.q: In this class, what do we learn about religions?
check.why: In public school we learn what each group believes. We do not say who is right.

review.q: The Qur'an is the holy book of which group?
review.why: The Qur'an is the holy book of Muslims, who follow Islam.

review.q: Who do Muslims believe God gave the Qur'an to?
review.why: Muslims believe God sent the words of the Qur'an to Muhammad.

review.q: What language is the Qur'an written in?
review.why: The Qur'an is written in Arabic and read from right to left.

review.q: From which side does a Qur'an open?
review.why: Arabic is read right to left, so page one is on the right.

review.q: What do many Muslims do before reading the Qur'an?
review.why: Many Muslims wash before reading. The washing is called wudu.

review.q: How is the Qur'an usually read?
review.why: Muslims recite the Qur'an out loud, and the voice goes up and down like a song.

chapters.title: Surahs and Ayahs
chapters.bigQuestion: How is the Qur'an put together, and how do children find their way around it?

story.title: A Bee and an Elephant
story.kicker: Yusuf finds two chapter names in the Qur'an that sound like a trip to the zoo.
paragraphs: Yusuf is in first grade. His aunt is teaching him to read the Qur'an. She opens the book to a page near the back. "This chapter is called The Elephant," she says. Yusuf laughs. "A chapter about an elephant?"
"Yes," his aunt says. "It tells about an army that came with an elephant. The Qur'an says God stopped them." The chapter is very short. It has only five lines. Yusuf can count them on one hand.
Then she turns to the middle of the book. "This chapter is called The Bee," she says. "The Qur'an says God taught the bee to build its home." This chapter is longer. Yusuf cannot count all its lines.

"Are there more animals?" Yusuf asks. "Yes," his aunt says. "There is The Cow. There is The Ant. There is The Spider, too." Yusuf wants to find every one. His aunt says he will learn the short ones first.
story.think: Why do you think Yusuf's aunt starts him on the short chapters instead of the long ones?

lessons.title: A Chapter Is a Surah
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an has 114 chapters, and each chapter is called a surah.
reading: Many books have chapters. The Qur'an has chapters too. A chapter of the Qur'an is called a *surah*. Say it like this: SOO-rah.
The Qur'an has 114 surahs. That is a lot! Some are very long. Some are very short. Each one has a name.
Muslims know many surahs by name. They say the name, not a number. "Let's read The Opening." "Let's read The Elephant."

words.d: a chapter of the Qur'an; there are 114 of them

look.title: How Many Chapters?
rows: Books in the Hebrew Bible (Jewish count)
look.cite: Standard counts: the Qur'an's 114 surahs; the Tanakh's 24 books; the New Testament's 27 books
look.prompt: Which of these holy books has the most parts? Which has the fewest?

check.q: What is a surah?
check.why: A surah is a chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114 surahs.

check.q: How many surahs are in the Qur'an?
check.why: The Qur'an has 114 surahs. Al-Fatiha has 7 lines, not 7 chapters.

check.q: How do Muslims usually name a surah?
check.why: Each surah has a name, like The Opening or The Elephant, and Muslims use the name.

lessons.title: A Line Is an Ayah
lessons.mainIdea: Each line of a surah is called an ayah, a word that also means "sign."
reading: Each surah is made of lines. A line of the Qur'an is called an *ayah*. Say it: AH-yah. More than one are called ayahs.
The word ayah also means "sign." The Qur'an calls the sun a sign. It calls rain and birds signs too. Muslims believe every line is a sign from God.
Ayahs have numbers. So you can find any line. Surah 1, ayah 1 is the first line of the book. We write it like this: 1:1.

words.d: one line, or verse, of the Qur'an; the word also means sign
something that points to something bigger

look.title: Finding a Line
look.text: Picture a page with small numbers in little circles. Each circle comes at the end of a line. The numbers go 1, 2, 3, 4. If your teacher says "Find 1:4," you look for surah 1 and count to the fourth circle.
look.prompt: What does the number after the colon tell you? What does the number before it tell you?

check.q: What is an ayah?
check.why: An ayah is one line, or verse, of a surah.

check.q: What else does the word ayah mean?
check.why: Ayah also means sign. The Qur'an calls things like the sun and rain signs.

check.q: What does 1:1 point to?
check.why: The first number is the surah and the second is the ayah, so 1:1 is the first line of surah 1.

lessons.title: The Opening, Seven Short Lines
lessons.mainIdea: The first surah is Al-Fatiha, The Opening, and it has just seven ayahs.
reading: The first surah is called *Al-Fatiha*. That means The Opening. It opens the book. It has only seven ayahs.
In simple words, it says: praise God, who is kind. God is in charge of the big day to come. We ask God for help. Show us the good path.
Muslims say Al-Fatiha in every prayer. Many small children learn it first. It is the surah Muslims say most often.

words.d: The Opening, the first surah of the Qur'an; it has seven ayahs
to say good things about someone

look.title: The Opening in Simple Words
look.text: Praise God, who cares for the whole world. God is kind and gentle. God is in charge of the day of judging. We worship only God. We ask only God for help. Show us the straight path, the path of the people you have blessed.
look.cite: Qur'an 1:1-7, Surah Al-Fatiha (The Opening), put in simple words from the Marmaduke Pickthall translation, 1930
look.prompt: What does the surah ask God for? Find the line that asks for something.

check.q: What does Al-Fatiha mean?
check.why: Al-Fatiha means The Opening. It is the first surah in the Qur'an.

check.q: How many ayahs does Al-Fatiha have?
check.why: Al-Fatiha has seven short ayahs. The Qur'an has 114 surahs.

check.q: When do Muslims say Al-Fatiha?
check.why: Muslims say Al-Fatiha in every prayer, so many children learn it first.

lessons.title: The Cow and the Bee
lessons.mainIdea: Some surahs are named for animals, like The Cow and The Bee.
reading: Surah 2 is called The Cow. In Arabic that is Al-Baqarah. It is the longest surah. A story inside it tells about a cow. That gave it the name.
Surah 16 is called The Bee. In Arabic that is An-Nahl. The Qur'an says God taught the bee. It says the bee builds homes in hills and trees. It says the bee makes a drink that helps people.
A surah's name comes from one thing inside it. The whole surah is not about that animal. The name is like a label on a drawer.

words.d: surah 2, Al-Baqarah, the longest surah in the Qur'an
surah 16, An-Nahl, named for what it says about bees

look.title: What the Bee Was Taught
look.text: The Qur'an says God taught the bee to make its home in the hills, in trees, and in the things people build. Then it says a drink of many colors comes out of the bee, and there is healing in it for people.
look.cite: Qur'an 16:68-69, Surah An-Nahl (The Bee), put in simple words from the Marmaduke Pickthall translation, 1930
look.prompt: What is the drink that comes from the bee? Where does the surah say bees build their homes?

check.q: Which surah is the longest?
check.why: The Cow, surah 2, is the longest surah. The Elephant is one of the shortest.

check.q: What does The Bee say God taught the bee?
check.why: Surah 16 says God taught the bee to build homes in hills, trees and what people build.

check.q: Where does a surah's animal name come from?
check.why: A surah's name comes from one thing mentioned inside it, like a label on a drawer.

lessons.title: The Ant and the Elephant
lessons.mainIdea: The Ant tells of an ant who warned her friends, and The Elephant tells of an army that was stopped.
reading: Surah 27 is called The Ant. In Arabic that is An-Naml. It tells about King Sulayman (Solomon). A little ant saw his army coming. She told the other ants to hurry home.
Surah 105 is called The Elephant. In Arabic that is Al-Fil. It tells about an army with an elephant. The Qur'an says God sent birds and stopped the army.
Muslim tradition says this happened long ago. It was around the year Muhammad was born. That was about 1,450 years ago.

words.d: surah 27, An-Naml, with the story of an ant who warned her friends
surah 105, Al-Fil, a short surah about an army with an elephant
the Arabic name for King Solomon, who appears in The Ant

look.title: The Ant Speaks
look.text: The Qur'an says that when the army reached the valley of the ants, one ant called out. She told the ants to go into their homes, so that Sulayman and his soldiers would not crush them without knowing it.
look.cite: Qur'an 27:18, Surah An-Naml (The Ant), put in simple words from the Marmaduke Pickthall translation, 1930
look.prompt: What did the ant want the other ants to do? Why?

check.q: What did the ant in surah 27 do?
check.why: The ant told the other ants to go home so the army would not crush them.

check.q: Who is Sulayman?
check.why: Sulayman is the Arabic name for King Solomon, whose army appears in The Ant.

check.q: What does the Qur'an say stopped the army with the elephant?
check.why: Surah 105, The Elephant, says God sent birds and the army was stopped.

lessons.title: Long Ones First, Short Ones Last
lessons.mainIdea: The long surahs are near the front of the Qur'an and the short ones are near the back.
reading: The Qur'an is not in story order. It goes by size, mostly. The *long* surahs come near the front. The short surahs come near the back.
The Cow is surah 2. It has 286 ayahs. The Elephant is surah 105. It has only 5 ayahs. The very shortest surahs have just 3.
So if you want a short surah, turn to the back. If you want a long one, look near the front. Al-Fatiha is the one exception. It is short, but it comes first.

words.d: having many ayahs; the long surahs are near the front
having few ayahs; the short surahs are near the back

look.title: Counting the Lines
look.cite: Ayah counts by the standard numbering used in most printed Qur'ans (Cairo, 1924)
look.prompt: Which surah has the most ayahs? What happens to the numbers as the surah number gets bigger?

check.q: Where are the short surahs?
check.why: The Qur'an mostly goes long to short, so the short surahs are near the back.

check.q: Which surah has 286 ayahs?
check.why: The Cow, surah 2, has 286 ayahs and is the longest surah.

check.q: Which short surah comes first anyway?
check.why: Al-Fatiha has only seven ayahs, but it opens the book.

lessons.title: A Shelf of Drawers
lessons.mainIdea: The Qur'an is like a shelf of 114 drawers, and children open the small drawers first.
reading: Think of a big shelf with 114 *drawers*. Each drawer is a surah. Each drawer has a name on it. Inside are the ayahs.
The big drawers are at the top. The small drawers are at the bottom. A child opens the small drawers first. The Elephant is a small drawer.
Children learn the short surahs by heart. Then they learn longer ones. Some grow up to know all 114. A person like that is called a *hafiz*.

words.d: a box that slides out of a shelf; here, a way to picture one surah
a person who knows the whole Qur'an by heart

look.title: Which Drawer First?
look.text: Picture the shelf. A drawer near the top says The Cow. It is huge and heavy. A drawer near the bottom says The Elephant. It is tiny and light. A six-year-old walks up and reaches for one.
look.prompt: Which drawer does the child open first? What is inside it?

check.q: In the shelf picture, what is each drawer?
check.why: Each drawer stands for one surah. The ayahs are inside the drawer.

check.q: What is a hafiz?
choices: A person who knows the whole Qur'an by heart
check.why: A hafiz is a person who has learned all 114 surahs by heart.

check.q: Which do children usually learn first?
check.why: Children start with the short surahs near the back, like The Elephant.

review.why: A surah is a chapter. An ayah is a line.

review.q: How many surahs does the Qur'an have?
review.why: The Qur'an has 114 surahs. Al-Fatiha has 7 ayahs, and The Cow has 286.
Al-Fatiha, The Opening, is surah 1. It has seven ayahs.

review.q: Which of these is a surah named for an animal?
review.why: The Bee is surah 16. The Cow, The Ant and The Elephant are animal names too.
The Qur'an goes mostly from long to short, so the long surahs are near the front.

review.q: What did the ant in surah 27 tell the other ants?
review.why: The ant warned the others to go home so the army would not crush them.
